findings.title: getCalendarCredentials stores un-awaited Promises; other consumers of `.calendar` break
findings.body: `getCalendar` is now async, so `calendar` in the returned objects is a `Promise<Calendar|null>`. `getConnectedCalendars` was patched to `await item.calendar`, but any other caller of `getCalendarCredentials` that reads `.calendar` synchronously (e.g. availability or selected-calendar code) now gets a Promise, which is truthy and has no `.listCalendars` or `.createEvent`. The return type changed silently and the PR does not audit the other call sites.

findings.title: async forEach callback makes calendar/video deletions fire-and-forget; try/catch is ineffective
findings.body: `forEach(async ...)` does not await the callbacks, so the `try/catch` around it can never catch rejections from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`. Those become unhandled promise rejections, which can crash the Node process in some runtimes. Previously calendar errors thrown synchronously (e.g. in the constructor) were at least caught. The function also returns and sends emails before the deletions finish, and on serverless platforms the work may be killed after the response. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` inside the try.

findings.title: async forEach callback makes deletions fire-and-forget; try/catch is ineffective
findings.body: Same problem as in the vital reschedule: `forEach(async ...)` is not awaited, so errors escape the surrounding try/catch as unhandled rejections and the deletions may not complete before the function returns. Await them with `Promise.all` and `map`.

findings.title: async forEach in requestReschedule: deletions not awaited, errors unhandled
findings.body: Making the `forEach` callback async means calendar and video deletions run detached from the mutation. Rejections become unhandled, and the mutation may return, or the serverless invocation end, before the events are removed from external calendars. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.

findings.title: async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it has already been awaited, so recurring-event calendar deletions can be lost
findings.body: The recurring-cancellation branch uses `forEach(async (credential) => {...})` and pushes `deletedEvent` into `apiDeletes` only after awaiting `getCalendar` and `deleteEvent`. `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` snapshots the array before those pushes happen, so they are not awaited. Errors go unhandled and the handler can return before the calendar events are deleted. The old code had the same shape but ran mostly synchronously. Now that `getCalendar` is async, the race is real. It also pushes resolved values, not promises. Replace with a `for...of` loop that awaits, or push the promises.

findings.title: Dynamic imports are created eagerly at module load, so nothing is lazy
findings.body: Each entry is `import("./x")` evaluated immediately when the object literal is built. All ~29 app packages start loading as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported, and the promises are kept for the process lifetime. This defeats the purpose of async or lazy imports, since the load cost is paid at startup. A failing import also becomes a rejected promise at module-eval time, with an unhandled rejection if nobody awaits it, and every later `await appStore[x]` rethrows it. Use thunks such as `() => import(...)` or a lazy getter.

findings.title: Unknown app keys give a misleading or noisy result
findings.body: `await appStore[...]` on an undefined key yields undefined and falls through to the warn. Separately, `log.info("calendarApp", calendarApp.lib.CalendarService)` still logs on every call. This is minor, but the awaited module namespace is typed as a union of dynamic-import modules, which makes the `"lib" in calendarApp` narrowing fragile.
